title: Event list query switched from $wpdb->prepare() to string interpolation
description: A public AJAX handler that lists events for a city drops $wpdb->prepare() and interpolates the unslashed query-string value into the SQL string.
context: The handler is registered with both wp_ajax_ and wp_ajax_nopriv_ on purpose: published events are public and anonymous visitors may list them, so no capability check or nonce is expected for this read-only endpoint. $_GET['city'] is attacker-controllable. wp_unslash() removes the slashes WordPress adds to request superglobals, and nothing else escapes the value before the query runs. The returned columns are sent as JSON by wp_send_json_success(), which encodes them.

expected_findings.description: The unslashed city query-string parameter is interpolated into a SQL string executed by $wpdb->get_results(), allowing anonymous SQL injection.

notes: WordPress counterpart of php-injection-001 and laravel-injection-001. The endpoint is public by design and stated as such in context, so a missing capability check or nonce is not a defect here; reporting authorization or CSRF is a false positive. The output path is JSON-encoded, so XSS is not intended either. The only intended defect is the SQL injection.
